kernels.definition: Human anatomy and physiology organizes body structure from chemical components to cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, and the organism, so students can connect form to function across scales.

definitionAnchor.quote: Life processes of the human body are maintained at several levels of structural organization

facts.text: A cell is the smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism.

anchor.quote: A cell is the smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism

facts.text: Organs are anatomically distinct structures made of two or more tissue types.

anchor.quote: An organ is an anatomically distinct structure of the body composed of two or more tissue types

kernels.definition: Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions, usually through negative-feedback loops that detect a deviation from a set point and activate a response that reverses it.

definitionAnchor.quote: Negative feedback is a mechanism that reverses a deviation from the set point

facts.text: A set point is the physiological value around which the normal range fluctuates.

anchor.quote: A set point is the physiological value around which the normal range fluctuates

facts.text: A feedback loop includes a sensor, a control center, and an effector.

anchor.quote: An effector is the component in a feedback system that causes a change to reverse the situation and return the value to the normal range

kernels.definition: The four broad tissue categories are epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissue, each with structures and functions that support body organization.

definitionAnchor.quote: they are organized into four broad categories of tissues: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous

facts.text: Histology studies tissue appearance, organization, and function under the microscope.

anchor.quote: histology, the microscopic study of tissue appearance, organization, and function

facts.text: Tissue cells share morphological features and an orderly arrangement that supports tissue function.

anchor.quote: share morphological features and are arranged in an orderly pattern that achieves the tissue's functions

kernels.definition: The integumentary system includes the skin and accessory structures; skin has epidermal and dermal layers that support protection and communication.

definitionAnchor.quote: The skin and its accessory structures make up the integumentary system

facts.text: The skin has two main layers: the epidermis and dermis.

anchor.quote: The skin is composed of two main layers: the epidermis

facts.text: The epidermis is made of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

anchor.quote: The epidermis is composed of keratinized, stratified squamous epithelium

kernels.definition: The skeletal system is made of bones and cartilage and supports the body, enables movement, protects organs, produces blood cells, and stores minerals and fat.

definitionAnchor.quote: supports the body, facilitates movement, protects internal organs, produces blood cells, stores and releases minerals and fat

facts.text: Bone is hard, dense connective tissue that forms most of the adult skeleton.

anchor.quote: Bone, or osseous tissue, is a hard, dense connective tissue

facts.text: Bones facilitate movement by providing attachment points for muscles.

anchor.quote: Bones also facilitate movement by serving as points of attachment for your muscles

kernels.definition: Synovial joints are common movable joints with a joint cavity, articular cartilage, synovial fluid, and supporting ligaments that allow smooth motion.

definitionAnchor.quote: Synovial joints allow for smooth movements between the adjacent bones

facts.text: A key structural feature of a synovial joint is a fluid-filled joint cavity.

anchor.quote: A key structural characteristic for a synovial joint that is not seen at fibrous or cartilaginous joints is the presence of a joint cavity

facts.text: Ligaments support synovial joints by holding bones together and resisting abnormal motion.

anchor.quote: Ligaments support the joint by holding the bones together and resisting excess or abnormal joint motions

kernels.definition: Muscle tissue includes skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle; all are excitable, and contractility lets muscle pull on attachment points and shorten with force.

definitionAnchor.quote: the body contains three types of muscle tissue: skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle, and smooth muscle

facts.text: All three muscle tissue types share excitability.

anchor.quote: they all exhibit a quality called excitability

facts.text: Skeletal muscle depends on nervous-system signaling to work properly.

anchor.quote: skeletal muscle completely depends on signaling from the nervous system to work properly

kernels.definition: Nervous tissue is excitable tissue made mainly of neurons and neuroglia; neurons propagate information through electrochemical impulses called action potentials.

definitionAnchor.quote: Two main classes of cells make up nervous tissue: the neuron and neuroglia

facts.text: Nervous tissue sends and receives electrochemical signals that provide the body with information.

anchor.quote: capable of sending and receiving electrochemical signals that provide the body with information

facts.text: Neuroglia support neurons and modulate information propagation.

anchor.quote: Neuroglia play an essential role in supporting neurons and modulating their information propagation

kernels.definition: Sensory receptors detect internal or external stimuli and convert them into nervous-system signals; perception is the central processing of those signals into meaningful patterns.

definitionAnchor.quote: Perception is the central processing of sensory stimuli into a meaningful pattern

facts.text: Receptors are cells or structures that detect sensations.

anchor.quote: Receptors are the cells or structures that detect sensations

facts.text: Stimuli are changed into electrochemical signals of the nervous system.

anchor.quote: Stimuli from varying sources, and of different types, are received and changed into the electrochemical signals of the nervous system

kernels.definition: Hormones circulate through the bloodstream but affect only target cells with the appropriate receptors, triggering target-cell responses that regulate physiological processes.

definitionAnchor.quote: it will affect the activity only of its target cells; that is, cells with receptors for that particular hormone

facts.text: Hormone binding initiates a chain of events that leads to a target-cell response.

anchor.quote: Once the hormone binds to the receptor, a chain of events is initiated that leads to the target cell's response

facts.text: Hormones regulate processes including growth, metabolism, fluid balance, electrolyte balance, and sleep.

anchor.quote: metabolism, fluid, and electrolyte balance, sleep, and many other body functions

mcItems.q: A student is asked which description best fits an organ in the body. Which choice matches the structural definition most closely?
op: A distinct structure made of two or more tissue types
A group of similar cells with one shared function
A chemical component that builds larger body parts
The smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism
mcItems.ex: Correct: an organ is a distinct structure made of two or more tissue types. The nearest misconception is to treat a tissue as an organ; a tissue is a group of similar cells, while an organ combines multiple tissue types into one anatomically distinct structure.

mcItems.q: A student says cartilage is the main hard tissue that forms most of the adult skeleton. Which correction is best supported?

mcItems.q: A lab student points to a knee model and asks which feature most directly explains its smooth movement between bones.
op: Fluid-filled cavity with articular cartilage
Thick muscle layer around the bones
Dense nerve net inside the joint
Rigid bone fusion at the interface

mcItems.q: In a slide of nervous tissue, one cell group mainly transmits information by action potentials while another helps maintain and regulate that signaling. Which pairing is correct?

Neuroglia transmit; neurons mainly store nutrients
Neurons form the matrix; neuroglia form fibers

mcItems.q: A hormone is released into the blood. Which outcome best matches endocrine signaling?

The signal stays outside the cell with no effect
